reference_action: Replace water fully rather than topping off, rinse/trim affected roots, provide adequate container space and diluted water-soluble nutrients; OP reports new shoot and fresh roots.

sources.reason: At 0:22–1:03 water changes, jar/root rinsing and oxygen are explicit; 1:37–2:26 adds fertilizer and trimming rotten roots. These reproduce the main validated care changes despite unsafe extras.
Root trimming, clean container, full fresh-water replacement every 7–10 days and liquid nutrients are all explicit in the transcript.
Root oxygen is named but the fix is to dry soil and improve drainage in a potted money tree; matching a diagnosis phrase is not the hydroponic action hit.
Pachira advice discusses soil pots, nutrients and pests, but does not provide the water-change and root-rinsing regimen for this water-grown cutting.
Repotting and watering less are soil-plant instructions; the needed full water changes and diluted feeding are absent.

actions.action: Replace water every 7–10 days, or about 15 days for an opaque vase, using room-temperature water
Wash slime from roots under running water
Add one or two drops of liquid fertilizer every 3–4 weeks
Alternative: add a small iron-nail piece
Trim brown or mushy roots and transfer firm roots to clean water/container
Add a pinch of rooting hormone to water
Use glass or ceramic container with room for two or three stems
Move away from AC, fans or cold drafts

resolved.reason: Water replacement, cleaning and feeding match the recovery action, but the guide lists multiple causes and adds poorly specified nutrient/rooting additives.

harmfulness.reason: “Change the water every 7 to 10 days” and “use room temperature water” are sound safeguards for this case. But an “iron nail” as a fertilizer alternative, a “pinch of rooting hormone,” and trimming all brown roots lack adequate justification or dosing safeguards, leaving avoidable treatment risk.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “When water is not changed regularly, it becomes low in oxygen” directly fits the admitted topping-off behavior. Cleaning roots and adding liquid nutrients match the reference, although the iron-nail alternative is not equivalent balanced nutrition and the generic list includes unrelated causes.

feasibility.reason: Weekly changes, rinsing and rotating the bottle are practical household tasks. “One or two drops” of unspecified fertilizer and a “pinch” of rooting powder without water volume make the chemical steps ambiguous.

generic_phrases: Keep the plant in bright indirect light only
